correctness.summary: Run is an unimplemented stub: it initializes match[]=-1 and prices[]=0 and performs no auction iterations, so it never produces an assignment regardless of the cost matrix.
correctness.triggeringInput: cost (n*n row-major) = {0,5, 5,0}, n=2, match=stackalloc int[2], prices=stackalloc int[2]. Expected an optimal assignment (e.g. match[0]=1, match[1]=0); actual leaves match all -1.
correctness.rootCause: The auction bidding/price-update loop is missing; only initialization remains.
correctness.suggestedFix: Implement the auction algorithm: repeated bidding rounds where unassigned bidders compute best/second-best net value, raise prices by the bid increment (plus epsilon-scaling), and reassign objects until all bidders are assigned; write final assignment to match[].

perf.summary: Run is a stub that only initializes match/prices and never reads cost or runs the auction; the AggressiveInlining hint and cost/n parameters imply an unimplemented algorithm.
perf.currentCost: No algorithmic work performed; 'cost' parameter is unused, so callers get a no-op that returns nothing meaningful.
perf.proposedChange: Either implement the auction relaxation or mark the method clearly as initialization-only. If kept as init, the two init loops can be fused into one loop over i setting both match[i]=-1 and prices[i]=0 to halve loop overhead.
perf.rationale: Fusing the two independent O(n) init passes into one halves loop bookkeeping and improves cache behavior; currently there is only one loop already, so the main signal is that the algorithm body is missing.
perf.risk: Behavioral: implementing the algorithm changes outputs by design. The loop-fusion note does not apply (already a single loop); flagged primarily because the file appears to be an unfinished stub.
